In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear evidence of Bose-Einstein condensates in the pion-emitters of heavy-ion collisions.

the experimental data of the three-particle correlations and the experimental data of four-particle correlations are not in conflict with the condensation of pions in the EPG sources, but they cannot be used as a direct evidence of the Bose-Einstein condensate of pions in Pb-Pb collisions.
the multi-particle correlation analyses are consistent with the EPG model with condensation, and the experimental results are compatible with a condensation fraction of about 30\% in the EPG sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multi-particle correlations are useful to probe the condensation fraction in an evolving pionic source with Bose-Einstein symmetry.
the multi-particle correlations are sensitive to the source condensation fraction in the low transverse momentum interval of pions.

the multi-particle correlations can be used as a tool to study the condensation effect in high-energy heavy ion collisions.
